quote: 1. With each buy order I enter, I know the exact price where I am going to sell at a loss if things don't work out as expected. I define this price level before I get in.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 2. Everyone makes mistakes; that's unavoidable. But not correcting a mistake or minimizing the damage of a position gone wrong is completely under your own control. The big mistakes start out as small mistakes that were allowed to get out of hand. You must realize that big losses are a choice and take responsibility for controlling them.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 3. If it reenters its base, I have a rule to cut at least 50 percent of the position.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 4. I'm only rich because I know when I'm wrong.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 5. Growth comes at the expense of comfort.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 6. There is a lot more noise and movement in the market with high speed trading and computerized algorithms, but the stocks that have the biggest moves continue to have the same characteristics.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 7. I've never made a buy at a low that I didn't just feel terrible and scared to death making it. It's easy to sell at the bottom. You can go home that night and it relieves you of your nerves.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 8. It's better to lose correctly than to win incorrectly.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 9. I usually hold my big winners for about six to twelve months, stocks that aren't that strong about three months, and my losers less than two weeks.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 10. Hope is not a strategy.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 11. Those who succeed big at anything all have the same attitude: You keep going until it happens or you die trying. Quitting is not an option.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 12. Expectancy is your percentage of winning trades multiplied by your average gain, divided by your percentage of losing trades multiplied by your average loss. Maintain a positive expectancy, and you're a winner.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 13. The biggest mistake investors make is they invest in the present rather than forward looking and looking at where the puck is going instead of where the puck is.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 14. You want to get on board when institutional money is pouring into a stock and lifting it significantly higher.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 15. Figuring yourself out and developing a discipline are probably the most important things.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 16. I've learned many things from George Soros, but perhaps the most significant is that it's not whether you're right or wrong that's important, but how much money you make when you're right and how much you lose when you're wrong.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 17. It's like studying an animal; certain stocks have certain characteristics and a certain way of behaving. You need to recognize when those characteristics are changing and act accordingly.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 18. What I learned from George Soros was sizing is 70 or 80 percent of the equation.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 19. Earnings don't move the overall market; it's the Federal Reserve Board... focus on the central banks, and focus on the movement of liquidity... most people in the market are looking for earnings and conventional measures. It's liquidity that moves markets.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 20. If you want to mitigate risk effectively, you simply must acknowledge that stocks don't manage themselves. You're the manager, and it's up to you to protect your hard-earned capital.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 21. There's nothing new under the sun... things just repeat themselves over and over again. It's really identifying what has existed and what has happened in the past.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 22. If you look at what the Fed did, the radical gamble they took to get inflation up 30 basis points from 1.7 to 2, it's, to me, sort of a risk-reward bet. You bet 1 to lose 40? And they lost.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 23. This is the biggest redistribution of wealth from the middle class and the poor to the rich ever.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 24. The key is to see things as they are—operating in the now—without seeing things as worse than they are out of fear, or better than they are out of greed.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 25. I don't really like hedging. To me, if something needs to be hedged, you shouldn't have a position in it.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 26. The road to success in the stock market is not a system or strategy; it's within you, and it will be realized only to the extent that you are able to control and direct your emotions as you encounter challenges.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 27. I make my money on the few stocks a year that double and triple in price. The profits in those trades easily makes up for all the small losers.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 28. Traders have to take their ego and throw it in a trash can when walking into the trading day because they are going to be wrong.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 29. If you want to reap big gains in the market, make up your mind right now that you are going to separate trading from your ego. It's more important to make money than it is to be right.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 30. Soros has taught me that when you have tremendous conviction on a trade, you have to go for the jugular. It takes courage to be a pig.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 31. Bad news is sometimes the best buying opportunity life gives you.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 32. Amateurs think about how much money they can make. Professionals think about how much money they could lose.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 33. Trade what you see, not what you think.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 34. If you're extremely confident, taking a loss doesn't bother you.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 35. When I've looked at all the investors that have very large reputations — Warren Buffett, Carl Icahn, George Soros — they all only have one thing in common. It is to make large concentrated bets where they have a lot of conviction.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 36. Stocks should be at a profit the first day you buy them.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 37. Not losing big is the single most important factor for winning big. As a speculator, losing is not a choice, but how much you lose is.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 38. Soros is the best loss taker I've ever seen. He doesn't care whether he wins or loses on a trade. If a trade doesn't work, he's confident enough about his ability to win on other trades that he can easily walk away from the position.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 39. Looking at the biggest winners, we found that in many cases, the earnings had been on the table for a while.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 40. The first thing I heard when I got in the business - not from my mentor - was, 'Bulls make money, bears make money, and pigs get slaughtered.' I'm here to tell you I was a pig.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 41. You must adjust your risk as a function of potential reward.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 42. I try not to get too complicated. I look at the daily Dow and that works but it's not foolproof.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 43. Look at your own life. You can get so many stock ideas from just what you're buying. … From examining your own life, you can come up with unbelievable, great investing ideas.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 44. The way to build superior long-term returns is through preservation of capital and home runs.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 45. There's no reason you should always be long. If you're sure a bear market is coming — go to cash.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 46. Success in investing doesn't correlate with I.Q. once you're above the level of 125. Once you have ordinary intelligence, what you need is the temperament to control the urges that get other people into trouble in investing.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 47. In investing, when I hear the word 'conviction' I run like a deer. All the biggest financial collapses in history were caused by smart people with conviction. I would bet on a person with average intelligence that respects risk over a genius with conviction any day of the week.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 48. The cup-and-handle is one of the better ones but it does not show up nearly as often as people might think. A cup-and-handle really has to occur in a general market correction.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 49. My favorite quote of all time is maybe Mark Twain: 'Put all your eggs in one basket and watch the basket carefully.' I tend to think that's what great investors do.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 50. To have lasting success in the stock market, you must decide once and for all that it's more important to make money than to be right. Your ego must take a backseat.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 51. Learn to buy weakness and sell strength, and not buy strength and sell weakness; because you're just going to continue to get whipsawed.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 52. Calculating risks shrewdly is the main ingredient for consistent superior performance. Pros play percentage ball, and that's why, in the long run, they are more consistent than amateurs.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 53. Too many investors look at the present. The present is already in the price. You have to think out of the box and visualize 18-24 months from now, what the world is going to be and what securities might trade at.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 54. I look for support points that have held in the past or previous highs the stock has pulled back down on to.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 55. The wonderful thing about our business is that it's liquid, and you can wipe the slate clean on any day.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 56. The single most important advice I can give anybody is: Learn from your mistakes. That is the only way to become a successful trader.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 57. Virtually every superperformance phase in big, winning stocks occurred while the stock price was in a definite price uptrend. In almost every case, the trend was identifiable early in the superperformance advance.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 58. I think diversification and all the stuff they're teaching at business school today is probably the most misguided concept everywhere.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 59. If you're early on in your career and they give you a choice between a great mentor or higher pay, take the mentor every time. It's not even close.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 60. Your stop loss should be a calculation as a function of expected gain. Then you back into risk based on your own personal math. That's the holy grail; managing the risk/reward relationship.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 61. Trading without a stop-loss is like driving a car without brakes. Those who trade without stops, eventually stop trading.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 62. I think investment psychology is by far the most important element, followed by risk control, with the least important consideration being the question of where you buy and sell.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 63. One of my favorite patterns is the tendency for the markets to move from relative lows to relative highs and vice versa every two to four days... It takes several days of a market rallying before it looks really good. That's when everyone wants to buy it, and that's the time when the professionals, like myself, are selling. Conversely, when the market has been down for a few days, and everyone is bearish, that's the time I like to be buying.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 64. To compound your money, and not your mistakes, your goal is to buy on the way up—not on the way down.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 65. If you don't feel like a fool, you're not managing risk.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 66. You must have a love for the market in order to be successful in this game.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 67. Do not invest in the present. The present is not what moves stock prices.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 68. Long-term success in the stock market has nothing to do with hope or luck. Winning stock traders have rules and a well-thought-out plan. Conversely, losers lack rules, or if they have rules, they don't stick to them for very long; they deviate.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 69. I cut the losers very quickly. The maximum loss I allow is 7%.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 70. My results went from average to stellar when I finally made the choice that I was going to make every trade an intelligent risk/reward decision.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 71. It was all because I got emotional and dropped every tool of discipline I've ever had.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 72. When you tell yourself, I'm going to break my rule just this one time, you open the door to losing discipline, because it's never just 'one time.'
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 73. I've always loved to play games, and face it: investing is one big game. You need to be decisive, open-minded, flexible and competitive.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 74. Chart patterns are not the cause; they're the effect. Human behavior hasn't changed and isn't likely to change much in the future.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 75. You can tell a lot by volume. If the volume doubles one day and the stock moves to a new high, it is telling you a lot of people are interested in the stock and buying it.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 76. I believe that good investors are successful not because of their IQ, but because they have an investing discipline. But, what is more disciplined than a machine? A well-researched machine can make many average investors redundant, leaving behind only the really good human investors with exceptional intuition and skill.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 77. The best risk control is knowing what you are doing.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 78. You don't have to involve yourself in every market movement. In fact, you should not attempt to. Be an exacting opportunist. Be selective and pick your entry spots very carefully. Wait until the probabilities are stacked in your favor before you act.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 79. The first thing I do is figure out how much money I could lose.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 80. I like putting all my eggs in one basket and then watching the basket very carefully.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 81. If you want to be the best, you have to do things that other people are unwilling to do.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 82. There really is no intelligent reason to increase your trading size if your positions are showing losses.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 83. I study the market because I want to do it and because I'm fascinated to find out what makes the stock go up and what is going to be the next big winning stock.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 84. Concentrating your bets decreases your overall risk because where you tend to be in trouble is if you have 35 or 40 names. If you have a big massive position, it has your attention.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 85. Do your homework. Recap the day. What do I want to happen tomorrow? What happens if the opposite occurs? What happens if nothing happens? Think through all the 'what-ifs.' Anticipate and plan, rather than react.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 86. Soros's great gift was how to use leverage, and how much money to have down based on the risk/reward and your sense of conviction.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 87. The more disciplined you can get, the better you are going to do in the market.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 88. I put a lot more weight into how this stock is acting relative to the S&P — you can see real divergences when stocks are making new highs and the relative strength line is not.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 89. Practice does not make perfect. Only perfect practice makes perfect.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 90. With every trade I make, my approach is always 'risk-first.' By thinking and acting 'risk-first,' you know exactly what you stand to lose if you're wrong, which in trading is far more important than what you stand to gain if you're right, because if you lose all your chips, the game is over.
speaker: Mark Minervini
